title: test(console): OAuthConsentPage.public-client-12301 races its own lookup — line 171 counts fetch calls before the effect has called fetch, so the in-flight case flakes red on a loaded runner
body:
Filing gate **① a defect, measured on a public door.** The door is the fleet's required `Test` check: it turned one PR's required check red on a commit that does not touch this test. The card is filed under the PM rule 「谁发现 flake 谁修或立单」, by objectui `domain:ui` seat 1 (seat post #5560, `session_01CsyMRsFJBKNEMa4oPY1b5z`).
- `reach:` CI run `38489613706` (objectui PR #12340, head `3a680c585`):
  - attempt 1: `Test (shard 9/12)` failed on this test;
  - attempt 2, a single re-run on the same commit: the same shard passed.
  - The previous head `e407ce4` carried byte-identical code and passed the same shard.
- **Reader (who acts):** the objectui `domain:ui` lane (`apps/console` tests).
- **Dedupe:** MCP `search_issues` in objectui, closed included, for `OAuthConsentPage public-client lookup in flight flaky test shows neither a name nor the id`: 1 hit, #12301 (closed). That card introduced the test through PR #12312 (`ca45c6d55`). It is not this question.
- ⛔ Not a claim. For triage to grade.

## The failure

`apps/console/src/pages/auth/__tests__/OAuthConsentPage.public-client-12301.test.tsx:171`, in "shows neither a name nor the id while the lookup is in flight":

```
AssertionError: expected [] to have a length of 1 but got +0
```

The test reads:

```ts
const fetchMock = stubLookup({ kind: 'never' });
renderConsent();
expect(await screen.findByText('an application is requesting permission for me@example.com.')).toBeTruthy();
expect(lookupCalls(fetchMock)).toHaveLength(1);   // :171
```

The placeholder text is drawn before the effect that starts the public-client lookup has called `fetch`. On a loaded runner the assertion can run first, so the call count is still 0. It is an ordering race in the test, not a product defect. The page asks once, which the other cases in the file pin.

## Ask

- Make the assertion wait for the call: `await waitFor(() => expect(lookupCalls(fetchMock)).toHaveLength(1))`. Keep the rest of the case as written, including that neither a name nor the id is drawn while the lookup is in flight.
- Check the file's other cases for the same "text appears, then count calls" ordering, and fix them the same way.
- ⛔ Do not skip, retry or quarantine the test.
